en: The Method for Reciting the Vajra-Ayus-Dhāraṇī.
By [the one] who held the rank of Kaifu Yitongsisi, Teshen, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Duke of Sushan with a fief of three thousand households, recipient of the purple robe, posthumously titled Sikong, and conferred the honorary title Dajian.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Temple, who is correctly titled "Great and Vast Wisdom," by imperial decree:
I now rely upon the *Vajraśekhara-yoga Sūtra* and the Sambhogakāya Buddha Vairocana.
At the summit of the form realm, in the fourth dhyāna,
he attained perfect enlightenment;
he then descended from the golden jewel-peak pavilion atop Mount Sumeru.
All Tathāgatas throughout the entirety of empty space and the pervasive Dharma-realm gathered like clouds,
surrounding him on all sides,
speaking with one voice and in unison:
I only pray that the World-Honored One will turn the four kinds of subtle and profound, secret wheels of Dharma,
namely: the Vajradhātu Wheel and the Trailokyavijaya Command Wheel.
The wheel of universal subjugation,
and the wheel of the accomplishment of all aims and benefits—
these are the four wheels.
They emerge from the heart of Vairocana Tathāgata;
on each wheel there are thirty-seven noble beings,
each with their respective mantra, samādhi, and mudrā.
Maintaining majestic deportment and upholding the power of the vow of great compassion,
[he dwells] in both defiled Buddha-worlds and pure,
wondrous Buddha-worlds.
Whether manifesting or remaining hidden, he turns the wheel of benefit and bliss,
delivering all sentient beings in various different ways.
Thus, after Vairocana Buddha had received the requests of all the Tathāgatas, [he proceeded].
When he was about to turn the wheel of the Dharma,
he immediately entered samādhi and beheld that Mahesvara and other deities were stubborn and difficult to transform.
They cling to false views;
they are not my body of tranquil great compassion,
nor are they fit to be tamed by it.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Samādhi of Wrath.
From the five-peaked vajra-bodhicitta at his chest,
there issued forth the body of the Bodhisattva Trailokyavijaya-vajra, with four faces and eight arms, blazing with majestic power and so radiant as to be difficult to behold.
Having prostrated universally to Vairocana and all the Buddhas,
he said, "I pray only that the World-Honored One will instruct me as to what I should do.
The Buddha then addressed the Bodhisattva Trailokyavijaya.
"You have now subdued those gods who were difficult to tame,
causing them to take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha and resolve upon Bodhicitta;
all the gods have thus taken refuge."
Only Maheśvara, relying on his great majesty and power,
came to oppose him; [the Buddha] then subdued him with various sufferings by means of Trailokyavijaya.
Even unto death,
the Buddha Vairocana entered the samaya of compassionate great pity and proclaimed the Vajra-life Dharani.
He then entered the *vajrāyus-samādhi* and,
forming a mudrā, empowered the deity Maheśvara,
whereby he was restored to life.
Their lifespan will further increase;
they shall take refuge in the empowerment of all Buddhas and receive the prophecy of attaining the eighth stage.
The mantra of Vajrāyus is:
Oṃ vajrayuṣe svāhā. The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
If there are good sons or good daughters who receive, uphold, and recite [this mantra] three times each day, one thousand times per session,
all past karmic causes and conditions of evil deeds will [be purified].
Those with short lifespans or untimely deaths,
by upholding this dhāraṇī,
will have their karmic obstacles eliminated through the purification of their faithful mind.
Furthermore, their lifespan will increase.
If there are those who practice samādhi,
they shall not undergo transformation within the physical body born of their parents during their present life.
He attained the five supernormal powers,
traversing the void with mastery,
and expounded the gateways of samādhi.
Sitting in the full lotus posture with the body upright and the eyes closed,
place the two hands one upon the other below the navel.
Visualize all the Buddhas pervading the empty space before you.
With clear and distinct perception,
one should visualize within one's own body, at the heart, a full moon,
its radiance brilliant and translucent.
Above it is a five-pronged vajra,
its form gradually increasing in size until it is equal to one's own body;
this transforms into the Bodhisattva Trailokyavijaya.
Upon the crown is Vairocana Buddha.
From the Buddha’s entire body and all his pores,
there issues forth the consecration of nectar.
Visualize yourself entering into the heart.
Then, further visualize the Bodhisattva Vajrasattva and immediately form the mudrā of the Vajrāyus-bodhisattva-dhāraṇī.
Form two vajra fists with the index fingers interlocked, the right pressing over the left,
and place them upon the crown of the head.
Recite the Vajrāyuṣa Dhāraṇī seven times;
place it upon the forehead,
then divide it and tie it around the neck.
Straighten the two fingers and rotate them all over the body in the manner of donning armor.
The mantra for the armor is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-yoga-adhiṣṭhāna. By means of this seal,
one attains a body like adamant,
indestructible and free from all calamities and misfortunes.
Those who see it will rejoice and give rise to great reverence.
Next, the homa altar for averting calamities and prolonging life is described.
Prepare a single clean chamber.
To the east, install an image of the Bodhisattva Vajrāyus;
hang various banners and canopies.
Before the image, construct a square altar measuring three cubits on each side.
Dig deep and remove tiles, rubble, bone ashes, and all other impure substances.
If there are no such defiled objects in the ground, take the original soil back and fill it in.
If there is a surplus of soil, this is an auspicious sign of great fortune.
The dharma is easily accomplished.
If there are any impure substances,
one should immediately take clean earth from both banks of the river to fill them level.
Mix various fragrances with *gomaya* and smear them [on the ground].
In the center of the maṇḍala,
draw a one-and-a-half-cubit *vajra-kavaca* using white powder.
In the center, pierce a hearth,
half a cubit deep,
with a surrounding rim.
If one does not wish to pierce [the ground], one should install a fire-pit.
The practitioner sits before the fire-pit.
On all four sides of the mandala, one makes offerings of food, drink, various fruits, and so forth.
Place vases at the four corners of the altar.
Light charcoal in the hearth.
First, prepare twenty-one pieces of milky wood, ten finger-widths long and as thick as a thumb.
Dip both ends of the stalk with clarified butter,
recite the Vajrāyus-mantra,
and cast it into the fire.
Once it has become intensely blazing,
one should visualize an eight-petaled lotus within the fire,
and within the pericarp of that flower, one should visualize the syllable A.
The light shines everywhere,
and one becomes the Bodhisattva Vajrāyus.
Next, with the four characters of the four vidyās:
Invite the Bodhisattvas to enter the fire pit and receive various offerings; then,
with the right hand, form the half-vajra mudrā.
Sprinkle water on the fire to purify it.
Next, take a vessel and fill it completely with melted ghee.
Then, take a single stalk of fresh green kuśa grass.
Take ghee,
recite the Vajrāyus-dhāraṇī once,
and cast it into the fire.
Up to one hundred and eight stalks or one thousand and eight stalks.
Subsequently, cast into the fire various incenses, milk, and curd.
Once the recitation is completed:
Pour three full ladles of ghee into the fire;
do so at the beginning and at the end.
If one can perform this during the three months of the long fast, or on one's own birthday, [the merit shall be immeasurable].
By making such offerings,
one can eliminate calamities and increase one's lifespan;
the land will be peaceful and secure, free from all disasters and epidemics, and winds and rains will occur in their proper seasons.
The Method for Reciting the Vajra-Ayuṣ-dhāraṇī, wherein all worthy and holy ones protect that person.
